newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan plans ports' development beyond 2000.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan plans ports' development beyond 2000.

text.p: Pakistan has decided to develop two more ports besides Karachi Port and nearby Port Qasim to meet the future needs, Abdul Samad Khan, director general of the Board of Investment said on Sunday.

"Seaborne trade forecast for Pakistan by the year 2000 is 42 million tonnes and the projection by 2005, 2010 and 2015 are for 53, 71 and 92 million tonnes respectively," Khan told a seminar which was also addressed by a visiting eight-member British Ports Mission to Pakistan.
The mission is led by Henry Rowe of Posford Duvivier, an independent British firm of consulting engineers.
The mission during its seven-day tour will visit Pakistani ports and explore business opportunities.

Khan said Karachi Port, which handles 16.1 million tonnes of cargo, and Port Qasim with 6.2 million tonnes, were 45 km apart and their dredged channels impose limits on the size of the vessels that can use the ports. Moreover departures of vessels from Karachi Port are invariably restricted by tides.
"Therefore there is a need for additional ports to meet the challange of increasing seaborne trade," Khan said.
The government had decided to develop Keti Bunder Port and Gwadar Port, he said.
May Gibson, Acting British Deputy High Commissioner, called Pakistan a "significant trading partner" of the United Kingdom and said total trade between the two countries reached $1.1 billion in 1995.
She said there was, however, plenty of scope for further trade and investment, particularly in the ports sector where the United Kingdom can offer its expertise.
